explanation: The statement `Directed r (g ∘ f) ↔ Directed (g ⁻¹'o r) f` is definitionally true (`Iff.rfl`), since `Directed` unfolds to `∀ x y, ∃ z, · · ∧ · ·` on the values `(g ∘ f) x` and `(g ⁻¹'o r)` is `Order.Preimage g r` unfolding to `r (g x) (g y)`. I searched Mathlib for any other declaration stating this (grep for `directed_comp`, `comp_directed`, `Directed … ⁻¹'o`, `⁻¹'o … Directed`, `Order.Preimage` with `Directed`), and read all of `Mathlib/Order/Directed.lean`. The only related facts are `directedOn_image` (set/image version of `DirectedOn`), `isDirected_onFun` (`IsDirected ι (r on f) ↔ Directed r f`), `directed_comp_iff_of_surjective`, and `Directed.mono_comp`, none of which states the same result. Batteries contains no `Directed` at all. So no distinct Mathlib declaration states this theorem; the only occurrence is the theorem itself.
